title: Cash-for-information whistleblower programs: Effects on whistleblowing and consequences for whistleblowers

scopes.description: The supplied DHP Stata workflow prepares the district-year analysis panel and runs the 15 regressions for Tables 3, 4C, 5, and 6. The appendix's IA1–IA5 results and the datasheet's historical raw-data provenance are contextual; no extra programs or raw-source rebuild are inferred.

requirements.description: Case-level input `district_courts_all` (the code uses an extensionless Stata `use` path). The code reads Received_Date, Election_Date, Election_Decision, Total_Federal_Recovery, Relator_Share, and Judicial_District; it derives year/election date/invdays and case outcomes, filters missing/National Election_Decision rows, and collapses to Judicial_District × year. Case population, field types, completeness, and source period are unverified; district-year outcomes must support the 1994–2012 sample and the resulting panel must preserve the 1993 lag history. The code generates the MP/VI/GU 1993 and 2013 boundary rows after case aggregation; no 2013 raw case-record requirement is inferred.

District-to-circuit input `jd_to_circuit` (extensionless Stata `using` path), merged m:1 by Judicial_District and supplying circuit_court; the code overrides ARW to circuit 8. The using key must be unique and cover all case-panel districts. Actual mapping coverage and compatibility remain unverified.

routes.description: Catalog candidate only: FJC.APPEALS metadata lists numeric DCIRC and two-character DDIST on an appeals-record product. It is not the author mapping file; readable access, complete district coverage, code crosswalk to Judicial_District names, uniqueness, and historical compatibility are unverified.
routes.expected_period: No period is stated in the catalog; a derived mapping must cover every Judicial_District in the case panel.

requirements.description: Separate district-year input `district_variables.dta`, merged m:1 by Judicial_District and year before the second controls merge. Its actual columns and which consumed post-merge fields it supplies are unknown because the file is absent and the code whole-table merges both inputs. Verify its key uniqueness, types, coverage, and any overlapping names with `controls.dta`.

Separate district-year input `controls.dta`, merged m:1 by Judicial_District and year after `district_variables.dta`. Its actual columns and source ownership of downstream fields are unknown; do not assign labor_force_sum, civil_begin_pending, attorney_hours, unemprate, district_internal_report, or district_num_cases to either file until actual metadata is checked. Verify key uniqueness, types, coverage, and overlaps.

issues.description: The package contains no data files or related package candidate, although the supplied code directly reads four inputs. No exact prepared-file catalog alias or matching code-field catalog hit was found. FJC.CIVIL and FJC.APPEALS are catalogued candidates with different product fields, not verified substitutes; no access barrier is established. The four inputs' readability, population, join contracts, and period remain unresolved.

After merging district_variables.dta and controls.dta as whole tables by Judicial_District and year, the code consumes district_internal_report, district_num_cases, labor_force_sum, civil_begin_pending, attorney_hours, and unemprate. With both source files unseen, their field ownership, types, overlap, and complete year coverage cannot be assigned or verified.

The program writes MP, VI, and GU into fixed observations 1485–1490 at 1993 and 2013 before encode/tsset/tsfill. The unseen case-derived panel's row count and ordering determine whether these rows are additions or overwrite existing observations; this is unverified, not a confirmed failure.

evidence.description: The datasheet identifies the supplied Stata program's analysis tables and describes separate manual preparation for remaining analyses.
evidence.quote:
The steps necessary to process the data used in the final analyses are described in the Data Section
of the paper. Appendix table C. provides a description of the variables used in the empirical
analyses.

Item 5.
The enclosed Stata program (DHP_code_final.do) was used to prepare the final database and
conduct the analyses from Tables 3, 4C, 5, and 6.
For the remaining analyses, the raw data used to generate the final datasets were unstructured. For
example, we manually coded information from each lawsuit by reading scanned pdf copies of the
court filings. Similarly, we accessed a professional networking site and Smartlinx and manually
searched for each individual and manually coded the relevant information. Consequently, for those
analyses we do not have computer programs converting the raw data into the final data sets.

evidence.description: The program reads the district lawsuit file and uses its received/election dates.
evidence.quote:
use "district_courts_all" ,clear

gen countcase=1
gen year=year(Received_Date)

gen election_date = daily(Election_Date, "MDY")

evidence.description: The program aggregates cases by judicial district and year, merges a district-to-circuit mapping, and overrides ARW.
evidence.quote:
collapse (sum) settlecase countcase declinedd dismissedd intervenedd  noelectiond Total_Federal_Recovery Relator_Share (mean) invdays, by(Judicial_District year)

gen avgtime=invdays
replace avgtime=0 if avgtime==.

 ren countcase countcase_sum
 ren settlecase settlecase_sum
 ren declinedd declinedd_sum
 ren dismissedd dismissedd_sum
 ren intervenedd intervenedd_sum
 ren noelectiond noelectiond_sum
 
//merge with circuit court
merge m:1 Judicial_District using "jd_to_circuit",nogen
replace circuit_court=8 if Judicial_District=="ARW"

evidence.description: The program sets six MP/VI/GU boundary rows at 1993/2013, then encodes districts and fills the panel.
evidence.quote:
// the panel has missing judicial-year for some districts which has 0 cases
//impute those missing district-year observations 
set obs 1485
replace Judicial_District = "MP" in 1485
replace year = 1993 in 1485
replace circuit_court = 9 in 1485
set obs 1486
replace Judicial_District = "MP" in 1486
replace year = 2013 in 1486
set obs 1487
replace Judicial_District = "VI" in 1487
replace year = 1993 in 1487
set obs 1488
replace Judicial_District = "VI" in 1488
replace year = 2013 in 1488
set obs 1489
replace Judicial_District = "GU" in 1489
replace year = 1993 in 1489
set obs 1490
replace Judicial_District = "GU" in 1490
replace year = 2013 in 1490

encode Judicial_District, gen(n_Judicial_District)
tsset n_Judicial_District year
tsfill
drop Judicial_District
decode n_Judicial_District, gen(Judicial_District)
order Judicial_District year

evidence.description: The program merges separate district variables and controls files and forms logged controls.
evidence.quote:
*** 2 - Merge controls (demographics and judicial resources) based on location information

merge m:1 Judicial_District year using "district_variables.dta", nogen

merge m:1 Judicial_District year using "controls.dta", nogen 

gen loglabor= log(1+labor_force_sum)
gen logcivilb= log(1+civil_begin_pending)
gen loghours = log(1+attorney_hours)
replace loghours=0 if loghours==.
replace logcivilb=0 if logcivilb==.
replace loglabor=0 if loglabor==.		
replace unemprate=0 if unemprate==.

evidence.description: The case input is filtered and converted into settlement and disposition indicators using the supplied election and recovery fields.
evidence.quote:
drop if missing(Election_Decision)
drop if Election_Decision=="National"

gen dismissedd=1 if Election_Decision =="Dismissed Pre-Election"
gen intervenedd=1 if Election_Decision =="Intervened"
replace intervenedd=1 if Election_Decision =="Partially Intervened"
gen declinedd=1 if Election_Decision =="Declined"
gen noelectiond=1 if Election_Decision =="Notice Of No Election"

replace dismissedd=0 if dismissedd==.
replace intervenedd=0 if intervenedd==.
replace declinedd=0 if declinedd==.
replace noelectiond=0 if noelectiond==.

gen settlecase=1 if Total_Federal_Recovery!=.
replace settlecase=0 if settlecase==.

replace Total_Federal_Recovery=0 if Total_Federal_Recovery==.
replace Relator_Share=0 if Relator_Share ==.

evidence.description: The supplied code constructs 7th, 8th, and 9th circuit treatment indicators and their union.
evidence.quote:
***Treatments
		 
 *9th circuit
gen nineshock =1 if circuit_court ==9
replace nineshock =0 if year <1994
replace nineshock =0 if year >2000 & circuit_court ==9
replace nineshock =0 if  nineshock==.

*8th circuit
		 
gen eightshock =1 if circuit_court ==8
replace eightshock =0 if year <2002
replace eightshock =0 if  eightshock==.

*7th circuit

gen sevenshock =1 if circuit_court ==7
replace sevenshock =0 if year <2007
replace sevenshock =0 if  sevenshock==.
		 
gen treat = sevenshock
replace treat=1 if eightshock==1
replace treat=1 if nineshock==1

evidence.description: The district ID is generated, the estimation sample is restricted to 1994–2012, and the panel is tsset by district-year.
evidence.quote:
bysort judicial_district: gen jdid = 1 if _n==1
 replace jdid = sum(jdid)
 replace jdid = . if missing(judicial_district)
 
*mark sample period

gen sample_period =1 if (year>1993  & year<2013)
 
tsset jdid year

evidence.description: The datasheet describes historical case, PACER, BLS, and DOJ collection as the provenance of data used in the study.
evidence.quote:
The list of whistleblower cases filed under the Fraud Claims Act was obtained from Engstrom
(2013), who collected the data through a series of requests to the DOJ under the Freedom of
Information Act. We manually obtained the court docket filing associated with each case from
Public Access to Court Electronic Records (PACER). We read each lawsuit and manually coded
information about the whistleblower, complaint process, companies’ reactions, and retaliation.
We obtained demographic information from the Bureau of Labor Statistics and information about
judicial resources from the Department of Justice.
We obtained information on career consequences from a professional networking site. We
manually reviewed each profile matched to a whistleblower and assessed the career consequences.

dependency_review.description: The frozen D0001 edge is the district_courts_all case-file read and is reviewed as R_CASES. Manual source review also finds direct reads of jd_to_circuit, district_variables.dta, and controls.dta; these are accounted as separate requirements without invented frozen dependency IDs.

actions.description: Identify and obtain the four compatible author-prepared inputs, or obtain enough exact source contracts to establish compatible routes. Use author-prepared analysis inputs as the primary route; the datasheet's historical FOIA/Engstrom/PACER/BLS/DOJ/network/Smartlinx provenance is not a set of mandatory AND inputs for this supplied program.
steps: Locate compatible author-prepared versions of district_courts_all, jd_to_circuit, district_variables.dta, and controls.dta; the assigned package inventory and related_packages list contain none. If no compatible release can be identified, request the exact input schemas, producers, and coverage instead of independently rebuilding unstructured historical data.

For district_courts_all, verify the code-consumed fields Received_Date, Election_Date, Election_Decision, Total_Federal_Recovery, Relator_Share, and Judicial_District; confirm date/type and election-category compatibility, target population, and 1994–2012 case-derived outcomes. Then verify the resulting panel has native 1993 rows/values needed by first in-sample lags; the code itself adds MP/VI/GU boundary rows at 1993 and 2013 after case aggregation, so do not assume 2013 raw case records are required.

For jd_to_circuit, verify unique Judicial_District keys, numeric circuit values, coverage of every case-panel district, and the ARW-to-8 override. FJC.APPEALS is only a catalog candidate with DDIST/DCIRC; use it only if a documented crosswalk, uniqueness, and complete district coverage are established.

Inspect district_variables.dta and controls.dta separately with bounded metadata reads. Resolve which file supplies each consumed field, any overlapping names, matching Judicial_District/year types, unique district-year using keys, and coverage needed for 1993 lags; preserve the code-generated 1993/2013 boundary rows without inferring extra raw-year requirements.

After collapse and the circuit merge, check the actual row count and ordering around observations 1485–1490 before the fixed MP/VI/GU 1993/2013 assignments; then check the resulting tsfill panel and 1993 values required by the first in-sample lags. Preserve 1994–2012 as the estimation sample.
validation: All four code reads resolve in one documented current working directory, and bounded source metadata matches the actual consumed fields and identifiers.
Both merge types are compatible; the using side is unique on Judicial_District for jd_to_circuit and on Judicial_District/year for each district-year file.
The estimation sample remains 1994–2012, native 1993 values support the first in-sample lagged specifications, and the source-generated MP/VI/GU 1993/2013 boundary rows remain in the panel.
Fields used after the two whole-table merges have verified file ownership, numeric/string types, nonconflicting names, and adequate year coverage.
The fixed assignments at observations 1485–1490 do not overwrite pre-existing districts; the tsfill-produced panel remains compatible with the 15 supplied regressions.

actions.description: After the input contracts and panel shape are verified, run the supplied entry point unchanged in a working copy with Stata 18, reghdfe 6.12.3, and ftools 2.49.1. All reads are relative to the current working directory; no execution or compatibility test was performed in this assessment.
steps: Copy the package into a working directory with the four verified inputs and make that directory the current directory before launching the code.

Run `do DHP_code_final.do` in Stata 18 with reghdfe and ftools available; retain the Stata session output for review. The source contains 15 reghdfe specifications and does not save/export the final in-memory panel or tables.
Review Tables 3, 4C, 5, and 6A–B against the paper after confirming all 15 specifications used sample years 1994–2012 and the prescribed treatment/circuit clustering definitions.
validation: Confirm the script completes all four reads and two district-year merges without changing source rows or merge semantics.
Confirm output includes 3 Table 3 models, 3 Table 4C models, 3 Table 5 models, 3 Table 6A models, and 3 Table 6B models.
Compare reported coefficients and sample sizes with the paper after input compatibility has been established; execution must not be treated as verified until a future authorized run succeeds.

review_notes: Scope covers only the supplied DHP_code_final.do workflow documented for Tables 3, 4C, 5, and 6. The appendix's IA1–IA5 results have no supplied executable programs and are contextual; no extra analyses are inferred.

All four direct data reads are separately accounted for. The frozen dependency checklist lists only D0001 for district_courts_all; manual source review finds the other three reads at lines 57, 91, and 93. No unsupported dependency IDs were invented.

The dependency graph for the supplied code is accounted for, but compatible input availability, schemas, field ownership, full coverage, and fixed-row panel shape remain unresolved. The sample is 1994–2012; validate 1993 lag values in the resulting panel, while MP/VI/GU 1993/2013 boundary rows are generated after case aggregation. The catalog and environment evidence are metadata/probes only, not proof of coverage or successful execution.

FJC.APPEALS is retained only as an unverified mapping candidate (DDIST/DCIRC). FJC.CIVIL is a catalogued federal civil docket candidate, not a verified equivalent for the FCA whistleblower case input or its election/recovery fields. Catalog misses do not establish license denial.

The authors' historical sources are provenance for their prepared data; they are not added as mandatory raw-source requirements. No author code, regression, data read, install, or source edit was executed or applied.

The supplied code emits regression output in Stata but contains no saved/exported final panel or table command; this output persistence limit is retained as context rather than an invented extra data blocker.
